Package hadur2.core.policy

Class PowerPolicy

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.policy.PowerPolicy
public final class PowerPolicy extends Object
When to fire full power instead of the gun's own choice, and, separately, when to fire less than it chose because a kill is already certain. Landing a power-3 bullet refunds 9 energy and deals 16, so against a gun that rarely hits us full power is energy-positive at any distance.
  • POW-1: where the profile rates their gun T0 and their energy exceeds 12, fire 3.0. A tier is only named once its own margin is narrow (see Tiers), so this is already DIAL-1's form.
  • POW-2: while this battle shows our rolling hit rate above OUR_RATE and theirs below THEIR_RATE, each by more than its margin of error (measured from the estimate's centre, see Estimate.center()), fire 3.0. Uncertain rates keep the gun's own power (DIAL-1).
  • POW-3: where the profile rates their gun T1, they are within POW_3_RANGE px and their energy exceeds 12, fire 3.0. A T1 gun is weak enough that closing the range already outweighs the energy risk, the same reasoning as POW-1 with one more tier and a range gate instead of an unconditional one.
  • POW-4: where no other rule applies and both rates are known within POW_4_MARGIN, fire whichever of the gun's own power or FULL_POWER gives the higher expected value (expectedValue(double, double)), our hit rate times the bullet's damage less the power spent. Robocode's damage curve is convex (its slope rises from 4 to 6 past power 1), so that expected value is convex in the power fired, and a convex function's best value over an interval is always at one of its ends — there is no point part-way between the gun's choice and full power worth checking.

Every full-power rule is still capped at a quarter of their energy, which is what kills them, so a finishing shot never wastes energy, and none applies while our own energy is MIN_OUR_ENERGY or less: there the gun's power-down in a losing energy war stands, because a full-power miss could leave us disabled.

POW-5 is the opposite kind of rule, a cap rather than a raise: while the enemy's gun tier is T3 and they are beyond POW_5_RANGE px, cap the shot at POW_5_CAP unless a full-power rule (POW-1 to POW-4, or RAM-1) already applies. A T3 gun is the opposite risk from POW-1/POW-3's weak guns: it is good enough to punish a heavier bullet's telegraphed extra turn time at long range, where the extra damage is worth less than the extra exposure, so the cap trades damage for staying less predictable rather than the other rules' trade the other way.

POW-5 is a cap, not a PowerPolicy.Reason, for the same reason END-3 is: it can only lower what was chosen, never raise it, so it is applied before the full-power rules (HadurCore calls capPower(hadur2.core.memory.Tiers.Gun, double, double) on the gun's own choice, then reason(hadur2.core.memory.Tiers.Gun, double, double, double, double, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate) and power(hadur2.core.policy.PowerPolicy.Reason, double, double) on the result) and a full-power rule that fires afterwards overrides it exactly as "unless a full-power rule applies" asks — power(hadur2.core.policy.PowerPolicy.Reason, double, double)'s Math.max against the gun's choice already ensures a full-power rule never ends up capped by POW-5 to something lower than what it or the gun would have chosen on their own.

END-3 is the opposite kind of override, so it is a separate calculation (leastPowerThatKills(double)) rather than a PowerPolicy.Reason: while their energy is at most a power-3 bullet's damage, the fight is already decided by whichever power is fired, so the least power that still kills spends no more energy than a kill needs. HadurCore applies it last, after power(hadur2.core.policy.PowerPolicy.Reason, double, double), capping whatever the gun or the rules above chose down to it — never raising it, so a shot the gun could already afford stays affordable.

HadurCore asks on every duel aim: the gun proposes a power, reason(hadur2.core.memory.Tiers.Gun, double, double, double, double, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate) says whether a policy overrides it, and power(hadur2.core.policy.PowerPolicy.Reason, double, double) gives the power the wave and the shot carry. Every method here is pure.

    • POW_4_MARGIN

      public static final double POW_4_MARGIN
      POW-4: both rates' margins must be at most this for the comparison to run. Set so a full HitWindow (100 outcomes) can actually reach it in the range where full power wins the comparison (above roughly 17% against a power-1 gun): at 0.05 its Agresti-Coull margin only closes that far below about 7% or above 93%, where full power practically never wins, so the rule could pass its unit tests (built from wider, unrealistic windows) yet never fire in a real battle.
      See Also:

  • Method Details

    • reason

      public static PowerPolicy.Reason reason(Tiers.Gun gunTier, double enemyEnergy, double ourEnergy, double enemyDistance, double gunPower, Estimate ours, Estimate theirs)
      The reason full power applies, or PowerPolicy.Reason.GUN to keep the gun's choice.

      Checked in order: our own energy first (at MIN_OUR_ENERGY or below nothing applies), then POW-1, POW-3, POW-2, then POW-4. POW-2 needs both rates known and each bound clear by a full margin: our centre less our margin above OUR_RATE, their centre plus their margin below THEIR_RATE. POW-4 needs both rates known within POW_4_MARGIN and the expected-value comparison (expectedValue(double, double)) to favour full power over the gun's own choice.

      Parameters:
      gunTier - the profile's tier for their gun; UNKNOWN unless its margin is narrow
      enemyEnergy - their energy at the scan, in energy
      ourEnergy - our energy, in energy
      enemyDistance - their distance at the scan, in px
      gunPower - the power the gun chose, for POW-4's comparison, in energy
      ours - our rolling hit rate on them
      theirs - their rolling hit rate on us
      Returns:
      which rule, if any, sets the power

    • capPower

      public static double capPower(Tiers.Gun gunTier, double distance, double gunPower)
      POW-5: caps gunPower at POW_5_CAP while gunTier is T3 and distance exceeds POW_5_RANGE, otherwise returns it unchanged. Never raises it, so a cheaper shot the gun already chose is never made more expensive; a caller applies this before reason(hadur2.core.memory.Tiers.Gun, double, double, double, double, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate)/power(hadur2.core.policy.PowerPolicy.Reason, double, double) so a full-power rule can still override it upward afterwards ("unless a full-power rule applies").
      Parameters:
      gunTier - the profile's tier for their gun; UNKNOWN unless its margin is narrow
      distance - their distance at the scan, in px
      gunPower - the power the gun (or an earlier step) chose, in energy
      Returns:
      gunPower, or POW_5_CAP if that is lower and the gate is met

    • power

      public static double power(PowerPolicy.Reason reason, double gunPower, double enemyEnergy)
      The power to fire: gunPower unless a reason applies, then FULL_POWER capped at a quarter of their energy, never below the gun's own choice.

      A bullet of power p takes 4p up to power 1, so a quarter of their energy is exactly a killing shot at 4 energy or less, and more than enough above that.

      Parameters:
      reason - the reason from reason(hadur2.core.memory.Tiers.Gun, double, double, double, double, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate)
      gunPower - the power the gun chose, in energy
      enemyEnergy - their energy, in energy
      Returns:
      the power to fire, in energy

    • leastPowerThatKills

      public static double leastPowerThatKills(double enemyEnergy)
      END-3: the least power that guarantees a kill on a hit, or Double.NaN when no single shot, even at FULL_POWER, would do it.

      Damage is 4p up to power 1 and 6p - 2 above it, so the inverse is taken on whichever segment their energy falls in, then clamped to a legal power. The result is never less than Rules.MIN_BULLET_POWER: a bullet that would need less than that to kill still needs firing at the minimum.

      Parameters:
      enemyEnergy - their energy, in energy; not negative
      Returns:
      the least power that kills on a hit, or Double.NaN if none does
